newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-BHP iron plant workers back on job.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-BHP iron plant workers back on job.

text.p: Construction workers building a A$1.5 billion iron plant for The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd (BHP) at Port Hedland, Western Australia, began to return to the work on Thursday after a three weeks strike, a BHP spokeswoman said.
The entire workforce of more than 600 workers, who walked off the job on January 2 over wage and benefit claims, is expected to be back on the job by Monday, she said.
The negotiator for eleven separate contractors in the Chamber of Commerce and Industry group had agreed to open talks, she said.
BHP hoped to still start production from the plant on schedule in December, with full production to start by mid-1998, she said.
The workers, with metals, electrical and crane drivers' unions, have been seeking up to 38 percent wage increases and A$500 a week living-away-from-home allowances.
They rejected a recommendation by the Industrial Relations Commission that they return to work earlier this month.
The plant will produce hot-briquetted iron pellets for use in steelmaking.
